title: How should an AI agent verify a sprite edit before applying it through MCP?
author: isberglabs
selftext:
Disclosure: I work on paid game-development tools. I’m interested in how MCP interfaces should handle generative-AI agents making changes to game assets.

For a sprite-sheet edit, an agent could identify a frame correctly and still damage its padding, alignment or neighbouring frames. A successful tool response alone would not establish that the result is usable.

One possible interface would let the agent inspect the sheet and frame coordinates, request an edit against a specific document revision, and receive a before/after preview before applying it. The host application could reject stale revisions and changes outside the selected region. An undo checkpoint would make accepted changes recoverable.

That leaves a practical question: how much should the host verify automatically? Dimensions, frame bounds and unchanged neighbouring pixels can be checked mechanically. Whether an animation still reads well requires viewing the result in motion.

This is a proposed design, not a report of a tested AI workflow. For people integrating agents into art tools, which checks have caught real mistakes, and where do you still require a person to review the result?
